title: The Jubilee
lead: Every seventh year the land rested and debts were released; every fiftieth year, the Jubilee, land returned to its families and Israelite debt slaves went free (Leviticus 25). The prophets and Jesus took up its language of release (Isaiah 61:1–2; Luke 4:18–19).

sections.b: Exodus commands a seventh-year rest for the land (Exodus 23:10–11), and Deuteronomy a seventh-year release of debts (Deuteronomy 15:1–11). Leviticus 25 adds the Jubilee, and 27:16–24 prices land by it. Jeremiah condemns Judah for taking back slaves after a release (Jeremiah 34:8–22), and Nehemiah makes the rich return land and cancel interest (Nehemiah 5:1–13). Chronicles counts the exile as the land's missed Sabbaths (2 Chronicles 36:21), and Daniel's seventy weeks extend the idea (Daniel 9:24). Isaiah 61 announces "release to the captives" and "a year of the LORD's favor," which Jesus reads at Nazareth (Luke 4:16–21). The Liberty Bell carries the words of Leviticus 25:10.
